module_title: Advanced PVC Techniques: Bending, Welding, and Fabrication

lessons.title: Heat-Bending PVC Pipes for Custom Angles
lessons.body: Heat-bending PVC lets you create custom angles without fittings, saving money and reducing joints where leaks can occur. You need a heat gun (or a charcoal stove with a metal sheet as a diffuser), a pipe cutter, measuring tape, marker, sand, and a bending jig or a simple wooden form. Work outdoors or in a well-ventilated area because PVC fumes are harmful. For pipes up to 50mm diameter, fill the pipe tightly with dry sand and cap both ends. The sand prevents the pipe from collapsing or kinking when heated. Mark the bend area with a marker â the heated zone should be about 3 times the pipe diameter on each side of the bend. For a 32mm pipe, heat a 100mm section. Use a heat gun on low setting, moving it constantly around the pipe. Heat until the PVC becomes flexible like rubber â usually 2 to 4 minutes. Do not scorch or burn the surface. Once flexible, bend it slowly against your jig or form to the desired angle. Hold it in place for 30 to 60 seconds until it cools and hardens. For a 90-degree bend, bend slightly past 90 degrees because PVC springs back a little. If you don't have a jig, you can bend around a bucket or a curved tree trunk. After cooling, remove the sand by tapping the pipe. Check for kinks or flat spots â if the pipe collapsed, cut off that section and try again. For large-diameter pipes (75mm and above), you may need two people: one to heat and one to bend. Always test-bend a scrap piece first to get the feel. In hot African climates, PVC softens faster, so reduce heating time. Store bent pipes away from direct sun to prevent warping. This technique is ideal for making custom angles for rainwater gutters, greenhouse frames, or solar panel mounts. Practice on short offcuts before working on a full length.

lessons.title: Butt-Welding PVC Pipes for High-Pressure Applications
lessons.body: Butt-welding PVC is different from solvent cementing. It uses heat to melt the pipe ends and fuse them together without any fitting. This creates a joint as strong as the pipe itself, capable of handling high pressure (up to 10 bar or more). You need a butt-welding machine (or a homemade jig with a heating plate), a pipe cutter, a facing tool, and a temperature gauge. The process: first, cut the pipe ends square using a mitre box or a pipe cutter. Then face the ends with a facing tool or a flat file to ensure they are perfectly flat and perpendicular. Clean the ends with PVC cleaner. Set the heating plate to 260Â°C (500Â°F). Insert both pipe ends into the heating plate until a bead of melted PVC forms around the entire circumference â about 1mm for small pipes, 3mm for larger ones. For a 50mm pipe, heat for about 30 seconds. Remove the heating plate and immediately push the two ends together with steady force. Hold for 30 seconds without twisting. The melted PVC fuses. Allow to cool for at least 5 minutes before handling. A proper weld has a uniform double bead around the joint. If the bead is uneven or missing, cut it off and redo. For high-pressure lines, always test the weld by filling with water and pressurizing to 1.5 times the working pressure for 1 hour. In Africa, where electricity may be unreliable, you can use a charcoal-fired heating plate, but control temperature with a laser thermometer. Butt-welding is used for irrigation mains, water supply lines, and industrial piping. It takes practice, so start on scrap pipes. Always wear heat-resistant gloves and eye protection. Never weld PVC that has been exposed to UV for years â it becomes brittle. Store welded pipes out of direct sun.

lessons.title: Fabricating PVC Fittings and Manifolds
lessons.body: Sometimes you cannot buy the exact fitting you need, or you need a manifold to distribute water to multiple lines. You can fabricate custom PVC fittings and manifolds using solvent cement, short pipe sections, and end caps. For a simple T-joint, cut a hole in the side of a pipe using a hole saw the same diameter as the branch pipe. Clean the hole and the branch pipe end with PVC cleaner. Apply PVC primer, then solvent cement to both surfaces. Insert the branch pipe into the hole and hold for 30 seconds. Wipe off excess cement. For a manifold, take a larger pipe (e.g., 50mm) and drill multiple holes along its length for smaller branch lines (e.g., 20mm). Use a drill press or a guide to keep holes perpendicular. Then cement short pipe stubs into each hole. Cap one end of the manifold and connect the other end to your water source. For a distribution manifold with valves, you can cement threaded adapters into each branch, then screw on ball valves. Always allow 24 hours for solvent cement to cure before pressurizing. For high-pressure manifolds, use butt-welding instead of solvent cement. A common African application is a manifold for drip irrigation: a 50mm main line with 10 branches of 16mm drip tape. Another is a manifold for a solar water heater, distributing hot water to multiple points. When fabricating, keep the manifold horizontal so air can escape. Use a spirit level. Test by filling with water and checking for leaks at each joint. If a joint leaks, cut it out and redo. Remember that solvent-cemented joints are strong but not as strong as butt-welds. For critical applications, reinforce with stainless steel clamps. Always work in a ventilated area and wear gloves and goggles. Store fabricated manifolds away from sunlight to prevent UV degradation.

lessons.title: Using PVC for Rainwater Harvesting Systems
lessons.body: Rainwater harvesting is vital in many African regions with erratic rainfall. PVC pipes are ideal for gutters, downpipes, and distribution lines because they are cheap, easy to work with, and resistant to rust. To build a system, start with your roof. Measure the roof area: 1 square meter of roof yields about 1 liter of water per millimeter of rain. A 100 square meter roof in a 20mm rainstorm can collect 2000 liters. Use 110mm PVC pipes cut in half lengthwise as gutters, or buy ready-made PVC gutters. Slope gutters toward the downpipe at 1cm per meter. Join gutter sections with PVC solvent cement or rubber couplings for expansion. The downpipe should be at least 75mm diameter to handle heavy flow. Use 90-degree elbows to direct water into a first-flush diverter. A first-flush diverter discards the first 1-2mm of rain, which contains dirt and bird droppings. You can make one with a 110mm pipe, a cap, and a small hole that drains slowly. After the first flush, water goes into a storage tank. Use a floating ball valve or a simple T-joint to divert. For the tank, use a plastic or concrete tank. Connect the downpipe to the tank inlet with a 75mm pipe and a mosquito screen. Overflow should be piped away from the foundation. For distribution, use 25mm PVC pipes buried 30cm deep to prevent damage. Add a tap at the end. In dry season, drain the system to prevent stagnation and mosquito breeding. Clean gutters before each rainy season. In coastal areas, use UV-resistant PVC (gray or white) to prevent degradation. This system can provide water for irrigation, livestock, or domestic use after boiling or filtering. Always keep a mesh screen on the tank inlet and inspect regularly.

lessons.title: Making a PVC Hand Washing Station (Tippy Tap)
lessons.body: A tippy tap is a simple hand washing station that uses a jerrycan or PVC pipe to dispense water with a foot-operated lever. It is ideal for rural schools, markets, and homes without running water. You need: a 20-liter jerrycan or a 110mm PVC pipe 60cm long, a 10mm PVC pipe for the lever, a rope, a nail, a candle, a knife, and a wooden frame or two forked sticks. If using a PVC pipe as the water container, cap one end and drill a small hole (2mm) near the cap for water to flow. For a jerrycan, drill a 2mm hole near the top. The tippy tap works by tipping the container forward with a foot lever. Build a frame: two forked sticks driven into the ground, with a horizontal stick across. Hang the container from the horizontal stick with a rope through its handle, so it can pivot. Attach a 10mm PVC pipe as a foot lever: tie one end to the bottom of the container and let the other end rest on the ground. When you step on the lever, the container tips forward, and water flows from the hole. Add a bar of soap tied to a string. Place a gravel bed or a bucket under the tap to catch wastewater. For a PVC pipe container, you can make a more durable tippy tap: cut a 110mm pipe 60cm long, cap both ends. Drill a 2mm hole near one end for water outlet. Drill a 10mm hole in the cap at the other end for filling. Use a 20mm PVC pipe as the pivot axis: drill holes through the container near its center and insert the pipe, then mount on a wooden frame. The foot lever is a 10mm pipe attached to the container. This design holds about 5 liters. In Africa, tippy taps are used in schools to promote hand washing. Use a clear plastic bottle to see water level. Replace water daily. Add a small amount of chlorine if water is not from a safe source. This project costs less than $5 and can be built in under an hour.

lessons.title: Project: Building a PVC Stand for a Water Tank
lessons.body: A sturdy PVC stand raises a water tank to create water pressure for gravity-fed systems. For a 1000-liter tank, you need a stand at least 1.5 meters high to provide about 0.15 bar pressure â enough for a shower or drip irrigation. Use 110mm PVC pipes for the legs and cross-braces. You will need: 4 lengths of 110mm pipe, each 1.5m long (legs); 8 lengths of 110mm pipe, each 0.8m long (horizontal braces); 4 elbow joints; 4 tee joints; PVC solvent cement; a saw; a measuring tape; and a spirit level. First, cut all pipes. Assemble the top frame: connect two 0.8m pipes with two elbows to form a square. Repeat for the bottom frame. Then attach the four legs to the corners of the bottom frame using tee joints. The tee joints allow the legs to pass through and also connect the horizontal braces. For the top frame, use elbows to connect the legs to the top square. Ensure all joints are square and level. Use solvent cement generously. Let it cure for 24 hours. For extra strength, add diagonal braces from the bottom of each leg to the opposite corner of the top frame. Use 45-degree elbows or just cut pipes at an angle and cement. Once assembled, place the stand on a flat, compacted surface. Fill the tank with water only after the stand is fully cured. For a 1000-liter tank, the total weight is about 1000kg, so the stand must be strong. If you are unsure, add more legs or use larger diameter pipes. You can also fill the legs with concrete for extra strength. In Africa, many communities use this design for rainwater harvesting or borehole water. Always test with a smaller tank first. Check for cracks or bending. If any joint leaks, cut it out and redo. Paint the stand with UV-resistant paint to prolong life. This project can be completed in one day with basic tools.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of filling a PVC pipe with sand before heat-bending?
options: A) To make the pipe heavier
B) To prevent the pipe from collapsing or kinking
D) To add color to the pipe
quiz.explanation: Sand supports the pipe walls from inside, preventing collapse during bending.

quiz.q: When heat-bending a 32mm PVC pipe, how long should the heated zone be on each side of the bend?
quiz.explanation: The heated zone should be about 3 times the pipe diameter on each side to allow a smooth bend.

quiz.q: Why should you bend PVC slightly past the desired angle?
options: B) Because PVC springs back a little when cooling
quiz.explanation: PVC has memory and tends to spring back slightly, so overbending compensates.

quiz.q: What is the recommended heating plate temperature for butt-welding PVC?
quiz.explanation: PVC butt-welding typically requires a heating plate at 260Â°C (500Â°F).

quiz.q: After pushing the heated pipe ends together during butt-welding, how long should you hold them without twisting?
quiz.explanation: Hold for about 30 seconds to allow the melted PVC to fuse properly.

quiz.q: What is a sign of a good butt-weld?
options: A) A single bead on one side
B) A uniform double bead around the joint
quiz.explanation: A proper weld shows a uniform double bead around the entire circumference.

quiz.q: When fabricating a T-joint from PVC pipes, what tool is used to cut the hole in the side of the main pipe?
quiz.explanation: A hole saw of the same diameter as the branch pipe creates a clean hole.

quiz.q: How long should solvent-cemented joints cure before pressurizing?
quiz.explanation: Solvent cement needs 24 hours to fully cure and reach maximum strength.

quiz.q: What is a common application of a PVC manifold in African agriculture?
quiz.explanation: Manifolds are often used to distribute water to multiple drip irrigation lines.

quiz.q: For a rainwater harvesting system, how much water can a 100 square meter roof collect from 20mm of rain?
quiz.explanation: 1 square meter yields 1 liter per mm of rain, so 100 mÂ² Ã 20 mm = 2000 liters.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a first-flush diverter in a rainwater harvesting system?
options: B) To discard the first dirty rainwater
quiz.explanation: The first flush discards the initial rainwater that contains dirt and bird droppings.

quiz.q: What slope should gutters have for proper drainage?
quiz.explanation: A slope of 1cm per meter ensures water flows toward the downpipe.

quiz.q: What is a tippy tap?
options: A) A type of water pump
B) A hand washing station operated by a foot lever
quiz.explanation: A tippy tap is a simple hand washing device that tips to dispense water when a foot lever is pressed.

quiz.q: In a PVC tippy tap, what size hole is typically drilled for water to flow out?
quiz.explanation: A small 2mm hole provides a controlled flow of water for hand washing.

quiz.q: Why is it important to add a small amount of chlorine to water in a tippy tap if the water source is unsafe?
quiz.explanation: Chlorine kills pathogens and makes unsafe water safe for hand washing.

quiz.q: For a 1000-liter water tank, what minimum height should a PVC stand be to provide adequate gravity pressure?
quiz.explanation: A height of 1.5 meters provides about 0.15 bar pressure, sufficient for many uses.

quiz.q: What is the recommended diameter of PVC pipes for the legs of a stand for a 1000-liter tank?
quiz.explanation: 110mm pipes are commonly used for strength and stability in such stands.

quiz.q: How long should you wait after solvent-cementing a PVC stand before filling the tank with water?
quiz.explanation: Solvent cement requires 24 hours to cure fully before bearing weight.

quiz.q: What is a good way to reinforce a PVC water tank stand for extra strength?
quiz.explanation: Diagonal braces prevent racking and add structural stability.

quiz.q: When heat-bending PVC, why should you work outdoors or in a well-ventilated area?
options: B) Because PVC fumes are harmful
C) To cool the pipe faster
quiz.explanation: Heating PVC releases toxic fumes that should not be inhaled.

quiz.q: What is the first step in butt-welding PVC pipes?
options: B) Cut the pipe ends square and face them
quiz.explanation: Square, flat ends are essential for a proper butt-weld.

quiz.q: Why is it important to clean PVC pipes with cleaner before solvent cementing?
options: A) To remove dirt and oils for better adhesion
B) To make the pipe shiny
quiz.explanation: Cleaner removes contaminants that can weaken the solvent cement bond.

quiz.q: In a rainwater harvesting system, what is the purpose of a mosquito screen on the tank inlet?
options: B) To prevent mosquitoes from breeding in the tank
quiz.explanation: A screen keeps mosquitoes out, preventing breeding in stored water.

quiz.q: What is the recommended burial depth for PVC distribution pipes in a rainwater harvesting system?
quiz.explanation: Burying pipes 30cm deep protects them from damage and temperature extremes.

quiz.q: What is a common material used as a water container for a tippy tap in rural Africa?
quiz.explanation: Jerrycans and PVC pipes are lightweight, durable, and readily available.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid butt-welding PVC pipes that have been exposed to UV for many years?
options: A) They become brittle and may crack
quiz.explanation: UV exposure degrades PVC, making it brittle and unsuitable for welding.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a spirit level when building a PVC stand?
options: A) To check for squareness and levelness
quiz.explanation: A spirit level ensures the stand is level and the joints are square.

quiz.q: How can you test a butt-welded joint for high-pressure applications?
options: A) Fill with water and pressurize to 1.5 times working pressure for 1 hour
B) Hit it with a hammer
quiz.explanation: Pressure testing at 1.5 times working pressure for 1 hour verifies joint integrity.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of fabricating custom PVC fittings instead of buying them?
options: B) They save money and allow custom sizes
quiz.explanation: Fabricating on-site saves cost and enables custom configurations.

quiz.q: In a PVC manifold, why should it be kept horizontal?
options: A) To allow air to escape
quiz.explanation: A horizontal manifold allows trapped air to escape, ensuring even water distribution.
